headline: SteelOrbis sees December US ferrous scrap holding firm-to-sideways
detail: SteelOrbis says domestic ferrous scrap could trend strong-sideways in December, carrying over November's upward momentum. For Chicago yards that points to steady-to-firm mill bids into the December buy rather than a pullback.

headline: Fund selling drives copper to a seven-month low
detail: LME three-month copper fell 5.5% to $12,502.50/t on Nov 18 and COMEX slid 5.9% to $5.63/lb, while LME cash dropped from $13,610 to $12,570/t even as LME stocks held near 327,500 t. Goldman estimates fund net longs fell from about 21% of open contracts to 9%, so the drop is speculative money leaving, which pulls copper scrap bids down with it.

headline: Copper steadies above $5.50/lb as traders ship US stocks to China
detail: COMEX copper held above $5.50/lb on Monday after last week's slide to a seven-month-plus low. Traders are now moving metal out of the big US stockpile to tightening China, reversing two years of tariff-driven flows into the US, which could narrow the US premium that has supported domestic scrap prices.

headline: Nucor lifts HRC spot price for an 18th straight week, to $1,310/st
detail: Nucor raised its hot-rolled coil consumer spot price $15 to $1,310 per short ton, and its CSI joint venture went to $1,380, with lead times of three to five weeks. Kallanish put domestic HRC at $1,350-1,400/st versus $830-865 a year ago, keeping EAF mills hungry for prime and shredded scrap.

headline: Fed's Waller says a half-point December hike may be needed
detail: Governor Waller said core CPI rising 0.3% for three straight months met his bar for a 50-basis-point move at the Dec 8-9 meeting, with the policy rate now at 3.75%-4%. Bigger hikes mean a stronger dollar and higher financing costs, both negative for metal prices and inventory carrying costs.

headline: US flat steel prices climb as scrap costs keep rising
detail: SteelOrbis reports US flat steel prices moving up even as weekly output rises, citing two straight months of scrap price increases. Firm finished-steel prices give mills room to keep paying up for scrap.

headline: Dollar heads for a fourth straight weekly gain near 104
detail: The dollar index neared 104 on Friday, its strongest since April 2025, helped by safe-haven buying during the AI-driven stock selloff and Waller's half-point talk. A strong dollar makes dollar-priced metals dearer abroad and weighs on scrap export demand.

headline: LME aluminum cash premium over three-month widens as stocks keep falling
detail: On Nov 18 LME cash aluminum rose to about $3,095/t while three-month fell to about $2,865/t, and opening stocks dropped to 220,350 t. A cash price well above forward shows physical metal is tight even as futures slide, which supports nearby aluminum scrap values.

headline: Platinum sinks to a 17-month low near $1,300/oz
detail: Platinum futures fell to about $1,300/oz, the lowest since mid-June 2025, on rate-hike expectations, weak auto demand and a 265,000-oz surplus expected for 2026. Lower platinum means lower payouts on catalytic converters.

headline: Palladium drops below $900/oz to a 19-month low
detail: Palladium fell below $900/oz, its lowest since April 2025, as hawkish Fed talk, sticky inflation and a firmer dollar hit the metal, with high financing and fuel costs threatening vehicle demand. Palladium is a key value driver in gasoline-car converters, so cat prices are likely to keep softening.

headline: Shanghai copper stocks nearly run dry even as funds dump copper
detail: Shanghai Futures Exchange deliverable copper fell to 27,642 t from a March peak of 433,458 t, the November contract jumped over 9% at expiry, and the Yangshan import premium hit a record $360/t. Physical tightness in China is the main floor under copper while funds sell, and it is pulling US stocks east.

headline: Gold rebounds about 2% to near $3,600 after its steepest weekly drop in months
detail: Gold rose about 2% to roughly $3,600/oz on Monday after Treasury Secretary Bessent warned against over-tightening, with markets at about 93% odds of a quarter-point December hike. Last week gold sank toward $3,500-3,540, its lowest since September 2025, as investors sold bullion to cover losses elsewhere.

headline: US raw steel output jumps 6% as utilization hits 81.7%
detail: AISI data show US mills made 1.886 million net tons in the week to Nov 14, up 6.0% from the prior week and 9.1% from a year ago, with capacity use at 81.7%. Higher mill run rates mean more scrap consumption heading into the December buy.

headline: October housing starts jump 9.9%, but permits fall 7.4%
detail: Starts rose to a 1.31 million annual rate, led by a 23.6% jump in multifamily, while permits fell 7.4% to 1.30 million and single-family permits dropped 8.7%. Falling permits point to weaker future demand for rebar, wire and other construction metal.

headline: European recyclers fight proposed EU limits on scrap exports
detail: Recycling Europe opposes an EU draft list that would restrict which non-OECD countries can import EU ferrous and aluminum scrap, saying about 20% of recycled steel and aluminum is exported and curbs could push scrap prices down. Fewer EU export outlets could change competition for US scrap in Turkey and Asia.

headline: Chile's 2026 copper output set for lowest level since 2003
detail: Cochilco expects Chilean output to fall 8.4% to 4.935 million tonnes in 2026, with only a 3% recovery in 2027; September production was down 15% year on year, with Escondida off 21%. Shrinking mine supply from the top producer limits how far copper can fall.

headline: China's October data miss: factory output +4.8%, retail sales +0.4%
detail: Industrial output growth slowed to 4.8% and retail sales to 0.4%, while fixed-asset investment fell 8.1% in January-October, all below forecasts. Analysts at ANZ expect no new stimulus this year, which leaves weak Chinese metal demand in place.

headline: China property investment down 21.6% in first ten months
detail: Official data show real estate development investment fell 21.6% year on year in January-October, new starts fell 24.4% and completions fell 26.6%. China's property slump keeps cutting demand for steel, copper and aluminum.
source: National Bureau of Statistics of China

headline: Push in Congress to repeal tariffs, including Section 232 metals duties
detail: A House bill from Reps. Beyer and DelBene would end Section 232 tariffs, which cover steel, aluminum, copper and other goods and apply to about 21% of US imports. Repeal is unlikely because Trump can veto it, so metals protection, and the US price premium it supports, likely stays.

headline: J.D. Power sees November auto sales at a 15.7 million pace
detail: November sales are forecast at about 1.2 million units, with a 15.7 million annual rate, down 0.2 million, record payments of $840 a month, and dealer inventory up 6.8% to 2.4 million. A steady but slightly softer build rate keeps prime busheling and end-of-life vehicle flows roughly flat.

headline: Silver falls below $42 to its lowest since September 2025, then bounces
detail: Silver dropped below $42/oz on Friday and was headed for a weekly loss of more than 13% on hawkish Fed signals and a stronger dollar, then rose more than 2% on Monday as hike bets eased. Big swings in silver affect values on silver-bearing scrap and electronics.

headline: Builder confidence falls to 25, lowest since April 2012
detail: The NAHB/Wells Fargo index dropped 4 points to 25 and 46% of builders cut prices, with mortgage rates above 7% cited; the Midwest reading fell 5 to 35. Weak homebuilding demand is a drag on construction steel and copper wire use.

headline: Codelco floats lower 2027 copper premiums for China
detail: Codelco is reportedly offering Chinese buyers $250-280/t premiums for 2027 cathodes, down from a record $350/t for 2026, while Freeport offered $158/t from its Indonesian smelter. Lower producer premiums signal less fear of shortage in refined copper next year.

headline: Copper treatment charges seen going negative for 2027
detail: The 2026 smelter treatment charge benchmark settled at zero, and in a Reuters poll 21 of 35 participants expected a negative 2027 benchmark of minus $50 to minus $150/t. Smelters paying to get concentrate shows how short mine supply is, a long-term support for copper and scrap.

headline: European aluminum premiums slide 12.6% as LME backwardation bites
detail: The Rotterdam duty-paid premium fell to $470-500/t from $540-570/t as a steep LME cash-to-three-month backwardation pushed stockholders to sell metal. Falling regional premiums are a sign that aluminum's physical squeeze is easing outside the US.

headline: Iron ore futures sink to a four-year low near CNY 650
detail: Dalian iron ore fell toward CNY 650/t, the lowest since October 2022, as China's October steel output dropped 1.6% to 70.83 million tons and supply from Australia, Brazil and Simandou grew. Cheap ore helps blast-furnace producers compete with scrap-fed mills.

headline: China holds lending rates at record lows for an 18th month
detail: The PBOC kept the one-year loan prime rate at 3.0% and the five-year at 3.5%, citing a stronger Q3 and firmer yuan despite weak October data. No new rate relief means no quick boost to Chinese metal demand.

headline: Canada extends tariff breaks for some Chinese steel and aluminum
detail: After Carney met Xi, Canada said it will keep exemptions for certain Chinese steel and aluminum products for two more years and add remissions for 32 more items, while US-Canada trade talks remain stalled since August. More Chinese metal into Canada could weigh on North American prices.

headline: US and Brazil baled scrap prices hold flat, with gains possible
detail: SteelOrbis reports BPI scrap prices unchanged in the US and Brazil, with no new deals confirmed and Brazil at $454/mt FOB, though a rise could come soon. Stable export bids for bales support prices for clips and new production scrap.

headline: Chinese automaker investment in Canada expected to play out over next year
detail: A Canadian official said Chinese investment in Canada's auto sector will develop over the next year; about 17,000 Chinese EVs have entered under a 49,000 annual quota, and Stellantis sold its Brampton plant to defense maker Roshel. Chinese auto production in North America would reshape parts and scrap flows near the US.
